name: Health Connect permissions
plain: A set of per-data-type read and write permissions for the health data store.
meaning: Each Health Connect data type (steps, heart rate, sleep, weight and more) has its own read and write grant plus background and history options. A privacy policy rationale page is mandatory.

android.prompt_ui: Health Connect permission screen with per-type toggles
android.persistence: Until revoked; Android 14+ is part of the system
android.store_policy: Play: Health Connect declaration form and policy review
android.note: Built into the framework on Android 14 (API 34); a Play download on Android 13 and earlier.

ios.prompt_ui: Health permission sheet with per-type toggles
ios.note: Clinical records need an additional capability and prompt.

limits.headline: Can see and add health data, one type at a time, from Health Connect or Health
limits.user_action: You tap Connect to Health Connect (Android) or Allow in the Health sheet (iPhone)
can: See steps, heart rate or other data types you switch on
Add new health data, such as a workout, for types you allow
Ask for background access and older history as separate permissions on Android
Use switches that you can turn off per type
cannot: See data types you left off
See older history on Android without the history permission
Tell on iPhone if you denied; it looks like no data
See medical records on iPhone without a second prompt
limits.reach_label: Only the data types you allow
limits.differs: Health Connect is built in on Android 14 and an add on for Android 13 or earlier. iPhone uses Health with the HealthKit setting.

story.what_it_is: Android's central store of health data with a permission for each kind.

marketing.name: Health Connect
marketing.pitch: Pitch: one place on your phone for health and fitness data, where you control which apps can read or write it.

story.for_you: Instead of one broad yes, you get a list: steps, heart rate, sleep, weight and more. You turn each on or off, and you can see which apps use them in Settings.
story.for_makers: Makers get one standard way to read and write data across fitness apps and devices. They must show a privacy policy page, and each data type needs its own approval.

use_cases.example: A running app writes your workouts so your other fitness apps see them.
A diet app reads your steps and weight to adjust your calorie goal.
A watch app syncs sleep and heart rate to the phone.
A walking game reads your steps to power up your character.
A sleep app reads your nights and writes a score.
A wellness program could read steps to give discounts if you opt in.
Health Connect rules ban selling this data to ad firms.

risks: Some apps ask for too much
story.android_note: Built into Android 14 and later, with a rationale page required for each app.
story.ios_note: iPhone uses HealthKit for the same job.

technical_bounds: Per-type grants; read and write separate
Android 16 ties sensor permission to this model
